newsitem.title: USA: CoVest Bancshares adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: CoVest Bancshares adopts rights plan.

text.p: CoVest Bancshares Inc said Wednesday it adopted a shareholder rights plan to discourage individuals or groups from acquiring large stakes in the bankholding company without first discussing their intentions with the company's directors.
CoVest, with assets of about $536.4 million, said the rights plan was not adopted in response to any specific event.
The plan provides for the distribution of one right on August 25, 1997, for each share of CoVest's outstanding common stock as of August 11, 1997.

In general, the rights plan provides that if a person, group or entity acquires a 15 percent or larger stake in CoVest or announces a tender offer, and CoVest's board chooses not to redeem the rights, all holders of rights, other than the 15 percent shareholder or the tender offeror, will be able to purchase a certain amount of CoVest's common stock for half of its market price.
The rights will expire no later than 10 years from the date of the plan's adoption, CoVest said.

"The Rights Plan was adopted simply as a precautionary measure to better position CoVest's shareholders to realize the long term value of their investment, and to provide an additional level of protection against coercive or abusive tactics," said CoVest President Larry Gillie in a news release.
